pl-l4d46c1-d1e115.summary: Asks whether the very wicked also feel God's mercy in some mitigation of punishment, so as to be punished less than they deserve.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e118.summary: Reports some who think they will have no relief, citing James: judgment without mercy for one who has not shown mercy.
claims: Some deny any mitigation for the damned.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e124.summary: Adds Augustine: mercy here, judgment in the future.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e134.summary: Adds Augustine on 'all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth': toward the saints all God's ways are mercy and truth, since he helps in judging and fulfills his promise in pitying; toward all he frees and damns, all his ways are mercy and truth, since where he does not pity, the truth of vengeance is given; 'where he does not pity' implies something done by God without pity.
claims: Where God does not pity, the truth of vengeance is given.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e146.summary: Objects with Cassiodorus on Psalm 50: these two, justice and mercy, are always joined to God's judgment; so even in punishing the wicked there is no justice without mercy.
claims: Justice is never without mercy in God's judgment.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e158.summary: Adds Cassiodorus: judgment and mercy are joined in mutual society, in which he briefly includes all God's works.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e164.summary: Quotes Augustine against those who say the damned's punishments will end: some vainly pity the eternal punishment of the damned with human feeling, softening hard sayings; they cite 'God will not forget to have mercy', but this concerns vessels of mercy; or if they apply it to all, they need not think the damnation of those going to eternal punishment can end, else the bliss of the just in eternal life could end too. But let them think, if they like, that the punishments of the damned are mitigated at certain times; God's wrath, their damnation, remains, but he does not withhold his mercies in his wrath, giving relief, not ending the punishment. Even exclusion from God's kingdom alone would be a punishment beyond any known torment; the eternal death of the damned will remain without end.
claims: Augustine allows that it may be mitigated at times.
Exclusion from God's kingdom is itself the greatest punishment.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e198.summary: Concludes that Augustine asserts the punishment of the reprobate will not end, while not rejecting that some relief be given; so it may be said that God, though he could justly, does not punish the wicked in the future as much as they deserve, but relaxes something, however wicked they are.
claims: God punishes the damned less than they deserve.

pl-l4d46c1-d1e201.summary: Interprets 'judgment without mercy for one who did not show mercy' as the judgment of damnation for one who was without mercy, or judgment without freeing and saving mercy, though he feels God's mercy in some alleviation. 'Mercy here, judgment hereafter' does not deny the effect of mercy in the future, freeing the elect and lessening the reprobate's torment, but contrasts how God now calls and justifies sinners, which he will not do then, when he will openly judge those he now judges secretly.
claims: 'Judgment without mercy' means without saving mercy.
Mercy now calls and justifies; judgment later is open.

pl-l4d46c1.summary: Asks whether the very wicked feel God's mercy in some mitigation of punishment. Some deny it, citing James's 'judgment without mercy' and Augustine's 'mercy here, judgment hereafter'. But Cassiodorus says justice and mercy are always joined in God's judgment, and Augustine, rejecting the view that the damned's punishment will end, allows that it may be mitigated at certain times, God's wrath remaining while relief is given. So God, though he could justly, does not punish the wicked as much as they deserve but relaxes something; 'judgment without mercy' means without saving mercy, and 'mercy here, judgment hereafter' contrasts present calling and justification with future open judgment.
claims: Their punishment may be mitigated, so they are punished less than deserved.
'Judgment without mercy' means without saving mercy.
Mercy and justice are joined in all God's judgments.
